Welcome—I'm glad you're here. Have you ever wondered why questions about faith, morality, and what’s truly right or wrong seem to echo through every age and culture? These are the kinds of questions that shape not just societies, but our personal stories, too.
In a world that’s so often split by doctrine and dogma, wouldn’t it be amazing to find some real common ground? Something deeper than just the boundaries of tradition? That’s exactly where C.S. Lewis takes us in his classic, Mere Christianity. He doesn’t just lay out a set of rules—he invites us into a living, breathing way of seeing what it means to be human, and how we fit into this big, mysterious universe.
Our journey together starts with a simple but powerful idea: there’s a kind of moral law, a sense of right and wrong, that seems to belong to all of us—no matter when or where we live. Where does that come from? And why does it matter so much?
As we go deeper, we’ll explore the heart of Christian belief—looking at the nature of God, our own imperfections, and the kind of transformation faith can bring. Lewis weaves together reason and spirituality, challenging our assumptions and shining a light on some of life’s toughest questions. And it’s not just theory—these ideas shape who we are, how we treat each other, and what it means to live a life full of meaning.
So, as we step into the pages of Mere Christianity, let’s ask together: not just what do we believe, but why does it matter? And maybe—just maybe—how these truths might help us find unity, purpose, and a little more hope along the way.
